findings.evidence: template/scripts/requirement_intake.py in the candidate diff: `return [ensure_project_membership(root, ref) for ref in sorted(refs)]` raises on the first RequirementIntakeError. The connected-adapter docs make `reconcile-board --all` the primary completion path. A single duplicate-item Requirement therefore blocks all later ones. Failing loudly is correct under the no-fallback rule, but the command could collect every failure and then raise once, naming each Requirement.
findings.summary: reconcile-board --all stops at the first Requirement whose membership cannot be confirmed, so the remaining Requirements are left unreconciled and the operator gets no per-item report.

findings.evidence: find_identical_open_requirement in requirement_intake.py compares only title and body after stripping the trailing Work identity line. A Requirement that is already in progress is reused silently. The design.md risk section accepts this, and the payload reports `reused`, so it is only a heads-up.
findings.summary: Rerun reuse treats any open Requirement with the same title and body as the same intent, regardless of its lifecycle stage or card status.
